tasks.short: Check load documentation for completeness and accuracy.

steps.what: Find the load-related documentation for the assigned journey.
Read document fields and compare consignment details with the transport assignment.

loop.input: Paper consignment images and known assignment fields; native digital fields bypass extraction.
loop.output: Candidate consignment fields with page regions, units, reservations and explicit unknowns.
loop.check: Driver checks extracted goods descriptions, quantities, units and reservations against the image; rules compare mandatory fields and assignment values. A numeric match alone never establishes the meaning of a reservation.
loop.stop: One extraction and at most one improved image; unreadable or ambiguous text goes to manual reading and planner clarification. Never guess a missing field.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native digital records and fixed rules handle structured inputs, but varied handwritten reservations and foreign paper layouts need bounded reading assistance.

steps.what: Resolve discrepancies and decide whether load documentation is accurate and complete.

tasks.design: Test native consignment packs in {OPS_SYSTEM} before custom integration. Reuse digital fields directly and use a bounded extraction only for paper; the driver verifies descriptions and reservations, resolves discrepancies and records the final check outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper and digital documents are mixed, with inconsistent descriptions and identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native digital consignment records reduce retrieval; bounded image extraction can assist with residual paper.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous reservations, unavailable documents and partner acceptance of electronic notes.
tasks.human_edge: Understand when a document misstates the actual consignment or needs planner intervention.

ambition.what: Identify incomplete consignment packs before reaching the collection point.

tasks.altitude: Less document hunting; responsibility to question an inaccurate pack stays with the driver.

reach.task: Prepare a missing-document exception for a collection.
reach.learn: Required document types and escalation contacts.

evidence.claim: TransFollow and Qargo support creation, issue and signing of electronic consignment notes inside the transport system, as described in the digest.
Model knowledge: bounded paper extraction can assist comparison but needs human checks of descriptions and reservations.

assumptions: Boundary is documentary checking, excluding physical cargo inspection and permission to drive. Planner clarification remains existing outside-role work, with additional extraction-related referrals budgeted below.

Planner supplies journey_id, consignment_id, sender, consignee, goods_description, packages, weight, units and required_document_types; shipper supplies document images and reservations. Missing or unreadable fields retain manual reading and partner clarification.
Test native digital packs first. Extraction does not create a legal original, infer signatures or authorize travel. All central savings are provisional model knowledge.
unknowns: Paper proportion, languages and native consignment support.
Partner document acceptance and access rights.
research_questions: Can extraction preserve reservation meaning and units on real paper notes?

incremental.description: Report extraction defects and obtain better images.
Maintain mappings and handle extra extraction referrals.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=60 gross=40 net=38 after 2 upkeep. Low: handwritten paper with frequent fallback; high: mostly digital packs and legible residual paper. Final discrepancy judgement stays fully human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect cargo to confirm it is secure.

steps.what: Inspect loads, restraints and load stability to ensure cargo is secure.

tasks.design: Keep cargo security inspection physical and driver-led. Check existing restraint guidance in {DOCS}; no camera judgement or digital checklist is credited with replacing the inspection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cargo stability requires direct inspection of a varied physical load.
tasks.enabler_now: No software breakthrough replaces that inspection in this design.
tasks.still_hard: Concealed movement, damaged restraints and unusual load geometry.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize unsafe loading and stop until it is corrected.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in inspection responsibility or safety decision rights.

reach.task: Explain a restraint concern to the loading crew.
reach.learn: Restraint limits and the agreed correction process.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: generic software does not replace a drivers physical cargo-security assessment.

assumptions: Boundary covers inspection only; restraint fitting, defect repair and documentary checking are separate and unchanged.

Loading team supplies the loaded vehicle and load characteristics; safety owner supplies current restraint guidance. Missing load characteristics require manual clarification before an assessment. No new structured interface or extraction is needed.
Review existing native guidance before considering code. Zero upkeep is justified because no new system or transferred work is introduced.
unknowns: Load types, access constraints and restraint guidance.
research_questions: Which unsafe conditions are hardest to observe physically?

incremental.description: No new system upkeep is introduced.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 upkeep=0 net=0. Both standard pallet loads and unusual cargo retain the complete physical inspection.

tasks.short: Obtain delivery signatures or receipts and collect required payment.

steps.what: Prepare the delivered-goods receipt for the consignee to check.
Check the delivered-goods statement and provide the required receipt or signature.
Collect any required payment and resolve payment discrepancies with the recipient.
File the signed receipt and payment outcome against the delivery.

tasks.design: Test native delivery receipt capture and attachment in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Prefill the delivered-goods statement, let the consignee check and sign its exact version, and file the signature and separately verified payment outcome against the delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signed paper receipts are filed after the delivery round.
tasks.enabler_now: Native electronic consignment signing can attach the final evidence directly to the trip.
tasks.still_hard: Recipient availability, disputed quantities, cash collection and offline delivery sites.
tasks.human_edge: Explain reservations without pressuring the recipient to sign an inaccurate statement.

ambition.what: Make a signed partial-delivery receipt available to finance during the delivery round.

tasks.altitude: Less filing at shift end; payment and delivery dispute rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Flag a delivery reservation that blocks invoicing.

evidence.claim: TransFollow and Qargo support electronic consignment-note creation, issue and signing inside the transport system.

assumptions: Boundary starts after physical unloading and covers receipt, conditional payment and filing; unloading is excluded. Shares reflect the mixed task portfolio, not a payment required at every stop. Customer signature time is outside focal B=75 and remains unchanged.

Planner supplies delivery_id, consignee, line_id and agreed charge; driver supplies actual_quantity, reservations and payment_status; consignee supplies signature and signing_time. Missing connectivity uses offline capture or paper with later manual filing.

Native capture first. Receipt v1 binds delivered lines, quantities, condition reservations and consignee identity; changes require another signature. Electronic documents are used only where accepted; no signature is inferred.
unknowns: Customer acceptance, offline coverage and payment collection frequency.
research_questions: Can offline capture preserve the exact signed version and avoid duplicate evidence?

already_counted.description: Review the delivered-goods receipt before signature.

incremental.description: Resolve failed uploads and missing evidence links.
Maintain document linkage and signing access.

approvals.approved_version: delivery receipt v1: delivery, lines, actual quantities, reservations and consignee; edits require new signature

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=75 R=45 gross=40 net=38 after 2 upkeep. Low: paper signatures and offline fallback; high: accepted native signing. Consignee signing and driver payment handling remain unchanged.

tasks.short: Maintain working-hours and vehicle service or repair logs.

steps.what: Record driving activity and vehicle movement in the tachograph.
Review working hours and enter required missing activity explanations.
Obtain the latest vehicle service and repair status.
Update vehicle service or repair logs and flag unresolved status discrepancies.

tasks.design: Test native tachograph exception views and vehicle service status in {OTHER} fleet recording software and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Reuse existing recorded activities and workshop status instead of copying them into a second log, while the driver confirms missing activity facts and unresolved repair status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Automatic activity data and workshop updates can be separated from the driver log.
tasks.enabler_now: Remote tachograph access and structured service states can reduce lookup and copying.
tasks.still_hard: Missing activities and uncertain repair release require truthful human correction.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize a status that does not reflect the actual vehicle condition.

ambition.what: Review unresolved service-status discrepancies before the next vehicle assignment.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated logging; no authority to override hours rules or workshop release is gained.

evidence.claim: Webfleet Tachograph Manager supports remote downloads, archiving and remaining-driving-time alerts, as summarized in the digest.
The digest identifies European driving-time and rest rules; the US state-and-federal wording is not applied to this European scenario.
Model knowledge: reusing structured workshop status can reduce duplicate service-log entry.

assumptions: Boundary covers driver review and log maintenance, excluding driving, workshop repair and compliance management. Existing tachograph runtime has 30 workflow units and no human saving; B=70.

Tachograph produces driver_id, vehicle_id, start_time, end_time and activity_code; workshop supplies job_id, vehicle_id, status, updated_time and authorized_release_reference. Missing feeds retain manual review and direct workshop confirmation, not guessed corrections.

Native configuration first. Driver entries cannot silently overwrite original activity records or authorize vehicle release. Access and national employee consultation are included; no driver ranking is proposed.
unknowns: Remote download support and service-status availability.
research_questions: Can the joined view retain original records and make every correction auditable?

already_counted.description: Review hours and missing activity facts.

incremental.description: Report feed mismatches and resolve new mapping exceptions.
Maintain record interfaces and access controls.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=70 R=37.5 gross=46.429 net=44.429 after 2 upkeep. Low: workshop facts remain verbal; high: structured status and supported downloads. Existing tachograph recording earns no new labour saving.

role.altitude: Spend less time hunting documents and copying log data while retaining physical safety checks and delivery accountability.
role.ambitious_version: A driver who can resolve documentary problems early without treating a digital record as proof of physical safety.
